chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the milk of the stallion (father). He (peace be upon him) said: 'What your wife breast-feeds from the milk of your child (breast-fed to a) child of another, so it is prohibited.'
ai.seo_question: How does a husband's milk establish kinship between children of different mothers?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the mechanism of 'radhāʿah' (milk kinship) by establishing that a husband's milk is legally attributed to his wife's nursing, thereby creating a mahram relationship between the children of different mothers who share his milk. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the biological father's milk serves as the primary source of kinship when the mother acts as the conduit, a principle derived from the Quranic concept of nursing establishing familial bonds.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Abdullah in Sinan who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the milk of the stallion (father). He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What your wife breast-feeds from the milk of your child (breast-fed to a) child of another, so it (brings about the) Prohibition’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu Najran from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the milk of ‘impregnating agent’.
He (the Imam) said, ‘It is the milk from your wife from your milk and the milk of your children given to the child of another woman and that child is unlawful (for marriage).”’
